securityNotes: Read SKILL.md in full at the pinned SHA. No markdown links present. Plain prose: turns knowledge gaps into research questions, matches questions to methods via a lookup table, requires an inclusion plan (participant diversity, method accessibility, situational context), and writes a research plan to a suggested repo path. No scripts, no network calls, no credential access, no hidden instructions. The 'Save to: docs/designpowers/research/...' line is a suggested output location for the calling project, not a read of any repository file, and the Integration footer's cross-references (inclusive-personas, design-discovery, design-strategy) are plain text, not links.

proposedEntry.name: research-planning
proposedEntry.description: Turns unclear user needs or contested assumptions into a structured research plan. Splits current understanding into known (evidence-backed), assumed, and unknown; converts gaps into 3-5 specific, observable, actionable research questions; matches each question type (what people do / why they struggle / what they need / which approach works / how they compare / who they are) to recommended methods via a lookup table; and requires every plan to address participant diversity, method accessibility, and situational context (stress, distraction, low bandwidth) rather than treating inclusion as optional. Outputs a research plan document with questions, a method/participants/timeline table, inclusion considerations, expected outputs, and the design decisions the research will inform. Explicitly scoped to planning only, not fielding the research.
triggers: we're making assumptions about users, plan research to validate them
what research method should we use for this question
turn these unknowns into research questions
inputs: A design brief or set of stated/unstated assumptions about users
Any existing evidence about the target users or context
outputs: Research plan document: research questions, method/participants/timeline table, inclusion considerations, expected outputs, decision points
